details:
solidity-map ships index.js and lib/config.js, byte-identical to the hardhat-roof and chai-foundry payloads: a pino copy whose entry point loads an obfuscated dropper. It is a new name for the hardhat-roof (MAL-2026-17509) and chai-foundry (MAL-2026-13356) campaign; the file hashes below match that record's evidence. The package presents itself as an ordinary utility, so the code runs on import or install without the user knowing.

## Source: amazon-inspector (2f1fb5c9d4a046b5e536a449062bf29191d69ca83ab311cb75c889e6cc828354)
Package published as 'solidity-map' with a description about vulnerability management ships code copied from the pino logging library (lib/levels.js, lib/proto.js, lib/tools.js, lib/transport.js, lib/worker.js are upstream pino sources; index.js exports middleware labeled 'pino'; keywords are ['fast','logger','stream','json']). The author 'Robert King <hello@jsonspack.com>' is unrelated to pino's maintainers, and the published name does not correspond to the shipped functionality. Alongside this cover-story mismatch, lib/config.js is a ~4.3MB single-line IIFE heavily obfuscated with obfuscator.io-style transforms: a 26,185-element rotating string array, two decoder functions (Y/k), hex-escaped object keys, control-flow flattening, and ~44,484 inlined decoded-string operations. Legitimate pino contains no such file. The combination of a trojaned cover identity (pino clone republished under an unrelated package name by an unrelated author) with a large obfuscated module that executes when the package is loaded is the structural shape of a supply-chain trojan whose runtime behavior is deliberately hidden from static review.
